key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even though point defects create deep gap levels, both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination are too weak to explain the observed photovoltaic efficiency losses.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, with defect management likely less critical than in many conventional semiconductors.
method: First-principles calculations of Shockley-Read-Hall recombination for a large, chemically diverse set of point defects.
Evaluation of both nonradiative multi-phonon emission and radiative defect-assisted capture.
Analysis of how recombination depends on defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a broad defect survey and finds large lattice reorganizations plus energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per recombination event, strongly suppressing SRH losses.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on calculated defect behavior, so real-device losses may still involve defect concentrations, microstructure, interfaces, or extrinsic effects not captured here.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
